notes: No numbered production cycle is active in pipeline/BRIEF.md; this proposal answers four direct Loremaster canon rulings (mother excised entirely, no dust in the shop, no family surname) that require rewriting already-shipped copy. Copy-revision only, no new reveals, no new runs or journal unlocks added. Two candidates per target, preferred marked with rationale. These rulings resolve ledger Open Questions 1 (who 'she' is, now moot), 7 (the dust-versus-nightly-diving timeline tension, now resolved by removing dust and keeping the death-to-run-1 gap short), and 8 (the surname Overby, now excised). The coordinator's own case-insensitive sweep confirmed the full footprint is story.ts lines 72, 73, 143, 248 plus journal.ts:65; all five lines are now covered as targets 1 through 4 below (target 1 covers story.ts:72-73, target 4 covers story.ts:143, target 2 covers story.ts:248, target 3 covers journal.ts:65). Gate verdict as of this pass: targets 1, 3, 4 approved (preferred candidates won). Target 2 was revised twice: the first-pass pair (run-end-3-revision-a/b, both built on 'quiet') was rejected for reusing vocabulary residue from the excised 'She took the car and the quiet with her.' line, which invited the reader to reconstruct the departure. Replaced with a third pass, run-end-3-revision-a2 (preferred) and -b2, which drop 'quiet', 'used to', and all before/after or change-of-state framing in favor of a present-tense physical image (bench, hour, block). One remaining out-of-scope conflict for the Loremaster's own pass, not rewritten here: lore/bible.md lines 47-48 ('The padlock is the only thing in the shop without dust on it.') and line 61 ('Family surname Overby...') still restate the old rulings and will need the Loremaster's own edit once the ledger update lands.

items.rationale: Mirrors the shipped beat's exact two-line, one-clause-each rhythm. Swaps 'under a decade of dust' for a clutter image tied directly to Dad (not Rhea, not time), and swaps 'without dust on it' for 'put away properly', which keeps the same job the line always had: the padlock is the one deliberate, cared-for exception in the room. No time markers, so it does not fight the short death-to-run-1 gap.

This candidate states only what IS, present tense: a physical fact about the bench and the hour, nothing about the house changing. Leaves the pull toward the machine entirely to the unchanged third line, 'The shop and I have some talking to do,' so nothing here duplicates or reinterprets that beat. items.title: THE DRAWER OF BILLS
items.rationale: Keeps the word 'Patient' so the sentence still names Dad as a patient, just by number instead of name. Reads a hair less cold than candidate B because 'Patient acct' is a hybrid, half-personal label.
items.notes: Replaces the existing journal entry id 'bills' (journal.ts line 65). Only the 'Patient: Overby.' fragment changes; body[1] and body[2] are verbatim, including the W-for-whatever filing joke, which stays as the son's own filing observation and is not tied to this account number.
body: MERIDIAN NEUROCARE - FINAL NOTICE. Patient acct: 118823. Diagnosis code NF-3, neurofilament degradation, stage three. Balance outstanding: more than this shop clears in a year.
There are eleven of these. He filed them under W for whatever.
Stage three of what? He fixed computers. He was not a diver. As far as I knew.

items.title: THE DRAWER OF BILLS
items.rationale: Drops 'Patient' entirely for 'Account No.', the coldest, most account-styled reading and the one that best matches a real hospital final-notice letterhead. Removes every trace of a personal identifier, which is the point of the ruling, and reads naturally next to 'Balance outstanding' two clauses later since both are billing-department language.
